title: Phantom Blade Zero Boss Order - All 60 Bosses in Progression Order

sections.title: Boss order at a glance
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero has 60 named encounters once you count optional and recurring fights: 33 story bosses that gate the story and 27 optional, recurring or rematch fights. You cannot miss a story boss; you can very easily miss the optional ones, because several expire at the Mount Soulrend climb.

The game is wide-linear rather than open world - each region is a hand-built map with a story spine and optional branches hanging off its bells. That means the order below is not a choice: region 9 is the last one, and the four bosses before the credits are fixed. What you actually decide is when to detour, since an optional boss you skip in Pangzhen is usually still available later, while one you skip in Meigu Lake may not be.

If you want the short version: fight every story boss in the order it appears, and take the optional fights in the region where you find them. The only optional encounter that is genuinely worth planning around is Blizzard Blademaster, which gates a true-ending branch.

sections.title: The last five, and where the credits actually fall
sections.content:
The endgame is fixed and short. Mount Soulrend is the point of no return: once you start the ascent, optional fights you left in earlier regions are gone, which is the single most common way people lose the true ending on a first run.

Leng Tu and Herald of the Veil come first, then Meng Hua at the peak - and Meng Hua is a true-ending checkpoint rather than a required fight. Zuo Shang, The True Long is the final boss. If the true-ending conditions were met, The Last Battle triggers immediately after Zuo Shang without a return to the hub; if they were not, the game ends at Zuo Shang and The Last Battle stays unplayed for that save.

Saw and the Crusher is the one optional encounter that sits after all of this, which makes it the last thing you can do in the game.

sections.title: How this list was built
sections.content:
Every entry comes from the site's boss database, which is the same source the individual boss pages render from, so the numbers here and the numbers on /boss-list come from one file rather than from two people counting separately.

Two limits worth stating. First, the count of 60 is a count of entries, not of unique characters: recurring fights and rematches are listed separately, and S-GAME's own public figure has been "50 or more" rather than an exact number. Second, phase counts and per-fight strategy are only recorded for a handful of encounters so far - where those fields are empty on a boss page it means the fight has not been documented here yet, not that the boss has no phases.
